question.prompt: Runnable web tests for this public home-page use-case need the page's starting URL, but no source line or existing variable supplies it.

options.label: Use new variable
options.detail: Author the tests against a new `{{home_page_url}}` variable and require the owner to fill it before execution.

options.label: Patch later
options.detail: Keep designing now and replace the missing URL in a later rework before the tests run.

options.label: Leave untestable
options.detail: Treat the missing home-page URL as blocking and leave the web tests as incomplete coverage.

gaps.risk_rationale: Without a start URL, the eventual browser tests cannot launch the home page even though the functional promises are otherwise specified.

judgements.rationale: Applied user-reach and change-frequency because this public landing-page route affects every visitor entering the publishing flow and homepage routing commonly changes during content iteration; did not apply auth or data-loss because the page is anonymous and read-only.

Applied money and user-reach because package pricing is a commercial promise shown to every prospective author on the public home page; did not apply auth or data-loss because no protected or mutable state is involved.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because this public route is a primary publishing navigation choice exposed to all visitors and is prone to homepage CTA updates.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because this public catalog route is exposed to all visitors and homepage outbound links are common content-touch points.

Applied user-reach because every visitor relies on the package preview set to understand the publishing offer; did not apply money because the count itself is structural rather than a monetary figure.
Applied user-reach because package names are essential orientation content for every prospective author viewing the landing page.
Applied user-reach because taglines are public discovery content that shapes package selection, but not money because the promise is descriptive rather than a numeric commercial term.
Applied user-reach because every public visitor needs the preview links to continue into package exploration from the home page.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the recent-books showcase is public discovery content and its membership changes as the catalog changes.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because broken recent-book title links strand public readers and the showcased books can rotate over time.
Applied user-reach and change-frequency because the catalog-size statement is a public credibility claim whose value changes as more books are published.
Applied user-reach because the main heading is the first public orientation cue on the landing page.
